inputs.sbc_source: SBC-zero market: Denka discloses no share-based compensation expense line. The only equity-award item is a ~JPY141m share-award provision on the balance sheet (<0.05% of revenue). SBC rows kept explicit at 0%; EquityAwardTaxes 0; house and street bases coincide.
inputs.fy_label_convention: CSV convention: FY label = calendar year the fiscal year ENDS (FY2026 = year ended 31 March 2026). Company materials label by START year (company 'FY2025' = CSV FY2026). All labels in this file use the CSV convention.
inputs.share_count_basis: 88,555,840 issued less 2,355,271 treasury at 30 June 2026 = 86,200,569 (Q1 FY2027 tanshin). No dilutive securities (annual report: 'diluted EPS not reported, no dilutive shares'). Held FLAT; buybacks are de minimis (JPY6m FY2026) and SBC is zero, so there is nothing to charge through the count.
inputs.net_debt_basis: 30 June 2026 balance sheet: short-term borrowings 58,347 + commercial paper 24,000 + current LT borrowings 15,250 + current bonds 15,000 + bonds 10,000 + LT borrowings 115,279 = 237,876 debt; cash and deposits 37,004; net debt 200,872. Lease obligations excluded (J-GAAP, leased assets only ~JPY3.4bn). Debt rose from 221,714 at 31 March 2026 (CSV FY2026 TotalDebt) on Q1 working-capital and capex funding.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in JPY, the currency of the flows. Cost of equity ~9.0%: 10y JGB ~1.7% + beta 1.2 x ERP 6.0% (cyclical specialty/commodity chemical, 47% market-value gearing). Pre-tax cost of debt ~1.4% (FY2026 interest expense JPY2.1bn on ~JPY220bn average debt), ~1.0% after tax. Market-value D/V is 47% today (JPY238bn debt vs JPY263bn market cap) but management's framework is net D/E <= 0.7x and gearing is expected to fall as the capex cycle normalises, so a forward weight of ~30% debt is used: 0.70 x 9.0% + 0.30 x 1.0% = 6.6%, rounded to 7.0%. No scenario-specific WACC and no ad-hoc risk premium: cyclicality, DPE and commodity risk are carried in the scenario flows and weights (risk charged once).
inputs.lease_treatment: J-GAAP filer; operating leases are expensed inside operating profit and finance leases are immaterial (leased assets JPY3.4bn). No lease adjustment: lease obligations are neither deducted from flows nor added to net debt.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, in the bridge: non-controlling interests of JPY27,085m (30 June 2026 book) deducted in equity_bridge. Flows are consolidated (100%), not attributable. NCI rose from 12,114 to 28,117 at March 2026 on consolidation of Toyo Styrene and Kainos Laboratories; book is a fair proxy because the FY2026 NCI loss (-4,443) was DPE's 30% minority absorbing wind-down losses, which do not recur in the flows.
inputs.non_operating_assets: Matching-asset rule: dividend income (JPY1,312m FY2026) and equity-method profit (JPY1,700m) sit below operating profit and are NOT in the EBITDA-built flows, so their source asset -- investment securities of JPY45,862m at 30 June 2026 (cross-shareholdings at fair value plus equity-method affiliates) -- is added in the bridge at 75% of book (25% haircut for tax on embedded gains and disposal friction). Management is actively selling cross-shareholdings (JPY13.6bn proceeds FY2026) to fund DPE wind-down costs, which is why both items sit side by side in the bridge.
inputs.interest_income_note: FY2026 interest income JPY328m is not stripped: the company is heavily net-debt (JPY201bn), so the cash pile is netted inside net debt rather than added as a separate asset, and the forward flows are built from operating EBITDA which excludes it anyway.
inputs.normalisation_note: FY0 reported FCF (-31,492) is NOT the projection base. FY2024-FY2026 were peak-capex years (cash capex 44.7 / 59.8 / 67.6bn, 11.5-17.6% of revenue, for the Thailand acetylene black plant and the SNECTON plant) and FY2025 carried a 16.1bn DPE impairment. The forward build normalises from components: EBITDA margin returning to the FY2016-FY2023 mid-cycle range of 13.8-16.6% (average 14.8%) plus the structural DPE removal benefit, with cash capex guided down to JPY47bn for FY2027 and converging toward D&A (7.5% of revenue) by year 4-5. Year-1 owner FCF is ~zero by construction, consistent with guidance (OCF ~JPY50bn vs capex JPY47bn).
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, component build, via the Drivers/build-dcf route. Routed as 'operating company, non-US cyclical' (SKILL.md row 2) -- a diversified Japanese specialty/commodity chemicals maker; adaptations applied: JPY-built WACC, J-GAAP no-lease-adjustment, NCI charged once in the bridge, cross-shareholdings added against stripped dividend/equity-method income, SBC-zero market (band_position null). Fresh build; no prior DCF and no memory entry. 10-year horizon because margins and capex are both still normalising from the FY2024-FY2026 investment cycle. Working-capital capture is NEGATIVE (-15% of revenue change): manufacturer with receivables + inventory well above payables. Cash tax ramps 28% -> 31% (Japan statutory ~30.6%) as the DPE loss carryforwards are consumed; FY2026 cash tax paid was only JPY2.7bn. Price is a regular TSE close, not volatile.

Q1 FY2027 tanshin. Flows are consolidated; NCI charged once here (Toyo Styrene, Kainos and other minorities).

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: equity_5yr_cagr (FY2021 267,448 -> FY2026 310,709). Used only as the long-run anchor; year-1 base growth of 13% is the consolidation step-up (Toyo Styrene, Kainos) against FY2027 guidance of +17.1%.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: EPS 5yr CAGR (-7.2%, FY2021 264.24 -> FY2026 182.10) diverges more than 30% from equity (3.0%) and revenue (1.6%). EPS is depressed by DPE: FY2025 was a loss year (-142.73) and FY2026 earnings include +12.6bn cross-shareholding gains and +8.2bn Ofuna land gain against -21.1bn DPE liquidation loss. Revenue is flat over 10 years (FY2016 369,853 -> FY2026 384,247): this is a no-growth top line with a mix shift underneath.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF = reported FCF (SBC zero, interest income not stripped). Capex is only available FY2024-FY2026 (-8,419 / -41,210 / -31,492, all negative), so no FCF CAGR is computable; the CapitalInvestment KPI (accrual basis) shows the pre-cycle run-rate was JPY21-42bn/yr (FY2016-FY2023) against OCF of JPY33-49bn, i.e. historical owner FCF of roughly JPY5-20bn/yr (1-5% of revenue) before the FY2024-FY2026 investment cycle. OCF FY2016-FY2022 averaged JPY41bn.

base.growth_rationale: Y1 13% vs guidance +17.1% to JPY450bn: H1 was revised down to 205bn (+4.2% YoY) and Q1 printed +3.1%, so the guided H2 (+30%) consolidation step-up is taken with some slippage. Y2-Y4 4-5% as SNECTON/filler volumes ramp on a flat commodity base, fading to 2% (JPY nominal) by Y8.
base.margin_rationale: Y1 14.0% ties to guidance (OP 30bn + D&A 32bn = 62bn on 450bn = 13.8%), below FY2026's 14.4% because the consolidated Toyo Styrene polystyrene revenue is low-margin and guidance carries a -5bn Middle East raw-material hit. Mature 16.0% = FY2016-FY2023 mid-cycle average 14.8% + ~1pp from DPE removal (segment loss -8.0bn in FY2025 vs +0.1bn FY2026) and the Best Practices cost programme (6.8bn targeted) + mix shift toward Electronics (13.9bn segment OP on 104bn sales in FY2026, growing), partly offset by Life Innovation normalisation.
base.capex_rationale: Y1 10.5% = guided JPY47bn investment on ~434bn revenue; falls to 8.0% (capex/D&A ~1.07x) by Y4 as the Thailand acetylene black and SNECTON plants are complete. The FY2016-FY2023 accrual capex averaged 8.3% of revenue, so 8.0% is a return to the pre-cycle norm, not a cut.
base.da_rationale: Guided FY2027 depreciation JPY32bn = 7.1% of 450bn; rises to 7.5% as the new plants depreciate, then holds.

bull.rationale: Guidance met in Y1 (+17%); Electronics & Innovative Products compounds high-single/low-double digits for five years as SNECTON becomes the de-facto low-dielectric standard and spherical silica/alumina ride AI packaging; group EBITDA margin reaches 18.5% (Electronics at ~25%+ OP margin on 40% of mix). Capex stays slightly higher for longer to fund the growth. Terminal growth 2% (Japan inflation).

bear.rationale: Guidance missed: Middle East raw-material disruption persists, the Q1 +6bn inventory effect reverses, Life Innovation test-kit demand keeps falling, chloroprene demand keeps declining and Chinese resin oversupply compresses Polymer spreads. EBITDA margin sits at the FY2024-FY2025 trough level (10.4-10.6%) plus the DPE benefit, ~12%; growth capex is cut back to near maintenance (7% vs 7.5% D&A). AI-materials demand grows but is too small to lift the group.

scenario_narratives.base: Denka is a flat-revenue, low-ROIC chemicals group (ROIC 2.5-7.3% FY2019-FY2025) with a genuinely good and growing electronics-materials business inside it. The base case assumes FY2027 lands modestly below guidance on the top line (consolidation of Toyo Styrene and Kainos adds low-margin revenue), the DPE closure benefit and the Best Practices cost programme lift mid-cycle EBITDA margin from the FY2016-FY2023 14.8% average toward 16%, and capex normalises from 17.6% of revenue to ~8% (capex/D&A ~1.07x) by year 4. Owner FCF goes from ~zero in year 1 to ~JPY29bn (5% margin) by year 10. The terminal value binds at the 15x cap. Equity value is net of JPY201bn net debt, JPY27bn NCI and an estimated JPY12bn of DPE wind-down cash costs, plus cross-shareholdings at a 25% haircut. The axes that matter are (1) whether EBITDA margin actually reaches 16% on a consolidated, lower-margin revenue base, and (2) whether capex really falls to 8% rather than a new Mission 2030 investment wave starting.
scenario_narratives.bull: The AI-materials thesis works: SNECTON is adopted as the standard low-dielectric resin for M9/M10-class CCL substrates, spherical silica/alumina fillers ride GDDR7/HBM and multilayer packaging, and acetylene black/ALSINK ride power-infrastructure and ESS demand. Electronics & Innovative Products grows to ~40% of sales at 25%+ operating margins, taking the group EBITDA margin to 18.5% by year 6 on revenue compounding 6-9% through year 5. The commodity segments merely stop shrinking. This is roughly the SBI Securities JPY4,400-target world, and it is the case the current price is paying for.
scenario_narratives.bear: The one-off-laden FY2026 recovery proves the high-water mark. The Q1 FY2027 inventory tailwind (+6bn) reverses, Middle East raw-material disruption lingers beyond October, Life Innovation's antigen-test demand keeps falling, chloroprene demand keeps declining and Chinese resin capacity compresses Polymer Solutions spreads. EBITDA margin settles at ~12% (trough FY2024-FY2025 levels plus the DPE benefit), revenue is flat, and growth capex is cut back to near maintenance. With JPY201bn of net debt and NCI ahead of equity, a 12% margin and ~JPY13-16bn of FCF leaves little or nothing for shareholders on a DCF basis: the bear case sits on or near the zero floor, which is the finding -- the balance sheet, not the P&L, is what makes this a leveraged bet on the electronics mix shift.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default 15/50/35 moved to 25/50/25. Bear up to 25%: market-value gearing is 47% (net D/E guided to 0.69x), owner FCF has been negative three years running, DPE's wind-down cost is open-ended and three of four segments are spread-driven commodity businesses -- a leveraged balance sheet on thin FCF makes a bad-cycle outcome materially destructive for equity. Bull down to 25%: it requires several independent things to go right at once -- SNECTON standardisation, sustained AI packaging demand, capex actually normalising, AND no commodity-spread relapse -- and the FY2027 guidance already embeds a Middle East drag and a 2H step-up management has not yet delivered.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF on normalised components, not on the latest FY's capex-depressed FCF. Denka's FY2024-FY2026 FCF (-8 / -41 / -31bn) is an investment-cycle artefact layered on a one-off DPE loss year; the normalised picture is a ~JPY400-450bn-revenue chemicals group earning a 14-16% EBITDA margin that converts to ~4-5% of revenue in owner FCF once capex returns to the ~8% pre-cycle norm. The market price (JPY3,055, 0.85x book, ~8x EV/EBITDA, ~16x guided P/E) sits between the base and bull values: the stock is priced for the AI-materials bull case, not for the mid-cycle base. The house view is not that the business is bad -- the electronics franchise is real -- but that with JPY201bn of net debt ahead of equity, the price already pays for the margin transformation before it has shown up in the group numbers.
key_risks_to_valuation: Base EBITDA margin of 16% assumes DPE removal + cost programme + electronics mix lift margins ~1pp above the FY2016-FY2023 average; if the consolidated Toyo Styrene revenue dilutes margin more than assumed, 15% would cut base value by roughly a quarter.

Capex normalisation to 8% of revenue is the single largest swing: Mission 2030 Phase 2 (FY2027-FY2029) could launch a second investment wave; every 1pp of permanent capex is ~JPY5bn/yr of FCF, ~JPY600-700/share at the cap multiple.
DPE wind-down cost (JPY12bn in the bridge) is an estimate with no disclosed total; a final decommissioning/remediation settlement could be materially larger or smaller.
Net debt is the June 2026 figure (JPY200.9bn), which includes Q1 working-capital seasonality; the March 2026 figure was JPY186.4bn (~JPY170/share difference).
The 15x FCF terminal cap binds in the base case (Gordon at 7%/1.5% would be ~18.5x); the cap is the house brake for cyclicals and is worth ~JPY400-500/share versus uncapped Gordon.
Bear scenario equity is at or near zero: the valuation is highly non-linear in the margin assumption because of leverage, so the weighted value is sensitive to the bear weight.
